claims: Diesel fuel is a refined petroleum distillate.
Diesel fuel is denser than gasoline.
Diesel fuel is more energy-efficient than gasoline.
Diesel fuel powers compression-ignition engines in trucks, buses, trains, and farm equipment.
Diesel fuel offers 11-40% better fuel economy than gasoline.
Common types of diesel fuel include Diesel #2 (standard) and Diesel #1 (winter/cold weather).
Diesel engines get up to 40% better mileage compared to similar gasoline vehicles.
Diesel fuel contains approx. 11% more usable energy per gallon than gasoline.
Diesel fuel has lower volatility than gasoline.
Diesel fuel is less likely to ignite than gasoline if spilled.
Diesel engines produce higher levels of nitrogen oxides (NOx) and particulate matter (soot).
Diesel fuel can gel or wax in extreme cold, clogging filters and hindering flow.
Diesel had approx. $3.52/gallon pump price vs $2.81/gallon for gasoline in Jan 2026.
Diesel #2 is Grade 2-D.
Diesel #2 is the most common type of diesel fuel.
Diesel #2 is used for general transport and machinery.
Diesel #2 can gel in cold weather.
Diesel #1 is Grade 1-D.
Diesel #1 is lighter.
Diesel #1 has lower viscosity.
Diesel #1 is resistant to cold temperatures.
Biodiesel is produced from vegetable oils or animal fats.
Biodiesel is often blended with conventional diesel.
Diesel fuel is used in commercial trucks, buses, trains, and some cars.
Diesel fuel is used in agricultural tractors, construction equipment, and cranes.
Diesel fuel is used in generators for standby power and in remote locations.
Diesel fuel powers marine engines in ships and boats.
Diesel uses compression ignition.
Diesel engines have no spark plugs.
Gasoline uses spark ignition.
Diesel fuel is an oilier product compared to gasoline.
Diesel fuel is less refined compared to gasoline.
